name: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
description: AMASS is a large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 different optical marker-based mocap datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization using the SMPL body model. It contains more than 40 hours of motion data, spanning over 300 subjects, more than 11000 motions. The dataset includes SMPL 3D shape parameters, DMPL soft tissue coefficients, and full SMPL pose parameters including hand articulations.
creator: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, Michael J. Black
publisher: MPI for Intelligent Systems, Meshcapade GmbH, York University, MPI for Informatics
citeAs: Mahmood, N., Ghorbani, N., Troje, N. F., Pons-Moll, G., & Black, M. J. (2019). AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes. arXiv:1904.03278v1 [cs.CV].
rai:dataCollection: 15 existing optical marker-based motion capture datasets were unified using MoSh++, which converts mocap data into realistic 3D human meshes represented by the SMPL body model. Publicly available datasets were downloaded from the internet. Several other datasets were obtained privately or recorded by the authors (Dancers, Transitions, BioMotionLab and SSM). A novel dataset (SSM - Synchronized Scans and Markers) was also collected using an OptiTrack motion capture system synchronized with a 3dMD 4D body scanning system.
rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: During mocap sessions, markers may get occluded by the body due to pose. A coefficient q is introduced to handle missing markers: q = 1 + (x/|M| * 2.5), where x is the number of missing markers in a given frame and |M| is the number of total observed markers. This updates the pose prior weight as a factor of the number of missing markers.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Optical marker-based motion capture data from 15 datasets: ACCAD, BioMotion Lab, CMU, EKUT, Eyes Japan, HumanEva, KIT, MPI HDM05, MPI Limits, MPI MoSh, SFU, SSM, TCD Hand, TotalCapture, and Transitions. Marker sets range from 37 to 91 markers per dataset. The SSM dataset was recorded using an OptiTrack system with 24 Prime 17W optical mocap cameras and 67 reflective markers, synchronized with a 3dMD 4D body scanning system using 22 pairs of stereo cameras, 22 color cameras, and 34 speckle projectors.
rai:dataImputationProtocol: When no markers are present on the hands of recorded subjects, the hand poses are set to the average pose of the MANO model.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: MoSh++ was used to map marker data into SMPL pose, shape, and soft-tissue parameters. Due to inherent problems with mocap such as swapped and mislabeled markers, results were manually inspected and either corrected or held out. The method uses two stages: Stage I estimates body shape and marker locations from randomly chosen frames; Stage II optimizes pose and soft-tissue deformation for each frame of the mocap sequence.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: MoSh++ converts mocap marker data into SMPL body model parameters through a two-stage fitting process. Stage I uses 12 randomly chosen frames to estimate shape and latent marker positions. Stage II optimizes pose and soft-tissue deformation coefficients for each frame. Hyperparameters were tuned using cross-validation on the SSM dataset. A scaling factor b = 46/n is applied to handle varying numbers of markers across datasets. Threshold Acceptance method is used as a fast annealing strategy to avoid local optima.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: MoSh++ (extension of MoSh), SMPL body model, SMPL-H with MANO hand model, DMPL for soft-tissue deformations, Chumpy autodifferentiation package, Powell's gradient-based dogleg minimization
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly available at http://amass.is.tue.mpg.de. The authors plan to continuously incorporate more mocap data contributed by themselves and the community. MoSh++ makes it easy to add more data and the dataset will continue to expand.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Body shape parameters (16 dimensions), body pose parameters (90 dimensions including hand articulations), soft-tissue dynamics (8 dimensions). The dataset spans 346 subjects with varying body shapes. Two of the three SSM subjects were professional models who signed modeling contracts allowing release of their 4D scan data.
rai:dataSocialImpact: AMASS enables new applications that require large amounts of training data for animation, visualization, and generating training data for deep learning in computer vision. It can be used to generate synthetic training data for computer vision tasks and to train models that denoise mocap data.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset does not include ground-truth data for evaluating accuracy of hand articulation. Current runtime for MoSh++ is not real-time. The SSM dataset used for hyperparameter tuning used a standard 46-markerset, which may affect performance on datasets with very different marker configurations. The velocity constancy weights depend on mocap system calibration, optical tracking quality, data frame rate, and types of motions, and could not be optimized using just one source of data.
rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, and Validation for deep learning models of human motion; animation and visualization; generating synthetic training data for computer vision algorithms; human pose estimation; body shape reconstruction; soft-tissue dynamics modeling; hand articulation modeling.
